first_impression.reaction: Googled 'why do we have bridesmaids' on the train after my friend asked me to be one. First line repeats my question and answers it. Good. Takeaways are mostly what a bridesmaid does plus Queen Victoria trivia, not really the 'why', so I'd read section 1, enjoy the 'always a bridesmaid' bit, then jump to the FAQ and leave.

journey.quote: Why do we have bridesmaids? Because a wedding is easier, and happier, with people you trust beside you.
journey.reaction: Answer straight away, no fluff. That's all I needed really.

journey.quote: This guide follows the bridesmaid from the wedding feasts of classical Athens to Queen Victoria's twelve in white, then turns to the decisions in front of you now: maid or matron of honour, how many to ask, bridesmen, and asking friends to travel.
journey.reaction: Tells me what's coming. Long sentence for a phone screen, but I get the map.

journey.quote: A bridesmaid helps the bride before and during the ceremony, and the maid of honour is the most important of them.
journey.reaction: That's the 'what', not the 'why'. The nice one-liner from the intro (people you trust beside you) isn't in the takeaways, which is where I'd look if I skipped the intro.

journey.quote: Queen Victoria had twelve bridesmaids in 1840, all eldest daughters of peers, dressed in white to her own design.
journey.reaction: Twelve! Fun fact, I'd tell the group chat.

journey.quote: For a wedding abroad, ask attendants early and talk openly about travel, time off and who covers what before anyone books.
journey.reaction: Not my question. Feels like the site's business poking into the summary. Skimmed past.

journey.section: 1. Why do we have bridesmaids today?
journey.quote: Couples ask friends to stand beside them for the same reasons people always have: support, company and a witness to the moment.
journey.reaction: Heading is literally my search. Clear answer, short section. This is the bit I came for.

journey.section: 1. Why do we have bridesmaids today?
journey.quote: "Always a bridesmaid, never a bride" goes back to the 1880s, and the "often a bridesmaid" version spread through mouthwash advertisements from the 1920s.
journey.reaction: Mouthwash ads, ha. Didn't know that. Specific dates make it feel real.

journey.quote: At a Roman wedding, friends and clients of both families gathered in the house of the bride's father.
journey.reaction: Short enough that I didn't mind, but this is where I start thumb-scrolling.

journey.section: 4. Maid of honour or matron of honour: what is the difference?
journey.quote: So the difference is marriage, not rank.
journey.reaction: One line, done. My actual next question answered. Would tap this if I saw it in a jump list.

journey.section: 6. How many bridesmaids should you have?
journey.reaction: Direct, then a short bold list. Easy to scan.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, Smartraveller advises getting travel insurance whoever you are and wherever you are going, and treats the right policy as essential as a passport.
journey.reaction: Dated, which I like, but travel insurance on a 'why do we have bridesmaids' page? Way off my question. It's far down so it didn't stop me, it's just a lot of scrolling.

journey.quote: Yes. A bridesman takes on the same role on the bride's side, and many couples now have mixed wedding parties.
journey.reaction: Short and clear. FAQ is genuinely useful, I'd jump straight here next time.

journey.quote: Yes. Many couples marry with one attendant or none, especially at a small ceremony abroad.
journey.reaction: Good, a straight yes. Nice that it doesn't make you feel weird for not having any.

unanswered_questions: Is there a jump list? Ten sections plus an FAQ is a lot of scrolling on a phone to reach the FAQ or the maid of honour bit.
I've heard bridesmaids used to dress like the bride to confuse evil spirits. Is that true? The page doesn't say yes or no, and that's half of what people mean by 'why'.

turn_offs_found.quote: A bridesmaid helps the bride before and during the ceremony, and the maid of honour is the most important of them.
turn_offs_found.why: Key takeaways is where I look first, and none of the four bullets actually answers 'why'. The intro line about having people you trust beside you should be the first bullet.

turn_offs_found.quote: As at November 2026, Smartraveller advises getting travel insurance whoever you are and wherever you are going, and treats the right policy as essential as a passport.
turn_offs_found.why: The destination section is long and about insurance, passports and visas, which has nothing to do with my search. With no jump list it pads out the page between me and the FAQ.

would_share_with: My friend getting married next year; I'd send her the 'How many bridesmaids' and 'maid or matron of honour' bits
The bridesmaid group chat, just for the mouthwash ad fact and Queen Victoria's twelve

cta_reaction.why: I'm not planning anything, I just wanted an answer. The CTAs are near the bottom and low-key so they didn't bother me. Might tap the free magazine if it's actually free with no sign-up wall.

top_3_changes: Make the first Key takeaways bullet the actual answer: we have bridesmaids for support, company and a witness, people you trust beside you.
Add a short jump list after the takeaways so phone readers can go straight to maid vs matron of honour, how many, and the FAQ.
Either say yes or no on the 'confuse evil spirits' story people have heard, or keep the destination travel section tighter so the page feels less long for a simple question.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Priya, a casual Google searcher on a phone
No invented brand facts; missing info went to unanswered_questions
No requests for prices, sourcing lines or deferred title/business details
